chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, from one of his shaykhs, from Idris ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said:

O Ali, a need is Allah’s trust with His creatures. So whoever conceals it within himself, Allah gives him the reward of one who performs salat (prayer). But whoever discloses it to one who is able to relieve him and he does not do so, then he has killed him. Indeed, he did not kill him with a sword, nor a spearhead, nor an arrow, but he killed him by what he wounded from his heart.

key_terms.الْحَاجَةُ: a need or state of want
key_terms.قَتَلَهُ: has killed him, used here for grave moral harm
key_terms.قَلْبِهِ: his heart, referring to inner emotional injury
key_terms.كَتَمَهَا: concealed it and kept it hidden
key_terms.يُفَرِّجَ: to relieve, ease, or remove distress

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله teach about revealing one’s need and refusing to help the needy?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the dignity of the needy person’s state and presents personal need as a trust from Allah. It praises restraint and patience, while severely condemning the one who is capable of helping but refuses, describing such neglect as a form of killing through heartbreak.
